rationale: Ownership of communication_kernel_sum_ms is unchanged from current discovery (revision fc9ec3b1, no bundles installed): the objective is generated exclusively by the 13 fp32 c10d::allreduce_ bucket calls of DDP's final-micro-batch reducer - call d0938de87369efd500322679 (12 buckets x 7,087,872 elements = 28,351,488 B) and call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b (one 39,385,344-element = 157,541,376 B bucket) - both direct children of the single complete-workload project call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb); execution_timeline and nsys show exactly 13 NCCL kernels and no other NCCL device work in the step. The concrete failure being repaired (trial-43f18a5360, decision no_valid_parameter_candidate, step_ms 249.8 vs limit 144.8) is now attributed by measurement, not conjecture: binding_cost-2087a4f7 shows the additive legacy functional binding at those two allreduce_ sites alone costs +92.3/+100.8 ms of clean step time (passthrough 232.3/247.0 vs parent 139.96/146.20), and the added gloo barrier further inflated rank-0's kernel sum to 80.5/73.9/81.1 ms by propagating barrier release skew into the remaining 12 launches. That evidence excludes re-selecting the two allreduce groups as functional sites under the fixed legacy backend, independent of any implementation quality, and also excludes CPU-side barriers in the burst path; the earlier trial (5a705e709d) already excluded communicator rerouting and NCCL env forcing. What remains in-contract is the measured ~0.5-0.8 ms gap between the clean baseline objective and the intrinsic transfer floor: collective_calibration-1af5837f puts the warmed allreduce cost at exactly these sizes at 12x3.536+19.383 = 61.82 ms (rank 0) and 12x3.615+19.522 = 62.90 ms (rank 1), versus baseline samples 63.21/63.32/66.48 and 63.41/63.67/64.12; the metric (element-wise max, median of 3) is set by rank 1's median 63.67 = floor + 0.77 ms, concentrated as mid-burst kernel inflation (seq 26/28/29: +0.25/+0.35/+0.47 ms, closing bucket +0.12 ms) and correlated with rank 1's larger comm/compute overlap (20.4 ms vs rank 0's 8.8 ms), i.e. the late rank enters the burst with more local compute in flight and its NCCL kernels absorb both waiting and SM contention. Rank 0's larger first-kernel absorption (+1.4/+1.5/+4.7 ms, tracking the measured 10.34-10.67 ms CPU submit spread at sequence 21 and the 194.7 ms first-kernel wait in the nsys capture) does not set the median and cannot move the metric alone. The only editable boundary that can restructure step scheduling without touching the frozen DDP reducer internals, bucket configuration, communicator or metric definition - and that replaces the whole bundle so no functional sites and no inherited-site dispatch cost remain - is the complete-workload project group itself, a direct callable boundary per the binding contract.
hypothesis: A whole-bundle replacement of the complete-workload call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (direct callable, zero functional replacement sites, so no repeat of the measured +92-101 ms legacy dispatch regression) that keeps the accumulation semantics, the unmodified DDP reducer, the default NCCL process group, all 13 bucket allreduces, the timed zero_grad/step/synchronize boundaries and every numerical policy exactly as the source, but makes the CPU dispatch cost of the step's pure-compute segments near-constant and early on both ranks - for example by executing the first accumulation_steps-1 no_sync micro-batch forward/backward segments via captured and per-invocation-refreshed GPU work (static buffers copied from the current inputs, warm capture after the untimed correctness pass, recapture from request['workload'] dimensions for the held-out longer_sequence variant) while the final synchronized backward and its reducer burst stay eager and unmodified, with no barriers, no extra collectives, no comm hooks and no environment forcing. Because both ranks then reach the synchronized backward with minimal, rank-symmetric CPU launch jitter, the late rank (rank 1, which owns the metric) should enter the 13-collective burst with less queued local compute and less arrival skew, shrinking its measured mid-burst kernel inflation and overlap-driven contention toward the calibration floor: expected max-rank median from 63.67 ms toward ~62.9-63.3 ms (about 0.4-0.8 ms, bounded by rank 1's measured intrinsic floor), with clean step_ms expected at or below the 139.9-146.2 ms parent range against the 144.8 ms limit since replay removes rather than adds CPU dispatch work, and bit-identical numerics (same kernels, same order, same communicator) preserving exact_gradient_replica_check and all reference checks. Unknowns to be tested rather than assumed: whether rank 1's +0.77 ms excess is CPU-launch-side (addressable by this rewrite) or GPU/transport jitter and SM contention that no in-contract scheduling change can remove, in which case the run acts as a measured control that pins the in-contract floor; whether graph capture of the no_sync segments composes with gradient_as_bucket_view accumulation without perturbing allocator or timing definitions; and whether parent step-time variance (139.96 vs 146.20 in the AB/BA arms) leaves enough margin under the 1.05x constraint on noisy runs.
